name: Zimri
overview: Zimri was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Jehoadda. His lineage is briefly noted in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 8:36, providing a concise but clear placement within Israel's tribal structure. There are no additional notes expanding on his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Zimri means 'wild goats, sheep; possibly awe of YHWH,' reflecting Hebrew linguistic roots. This proper name, not given directly by God, appears in 1 Chronicles 8:36, indicating a personal name common among the Benjamite lineage without explicit divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zimri as the son of Jehoaddah and explicitly as the father of Moza, both relationships noted in 1 Chronicles 8:36. These connections place him within a familial line important enough to be preserved in the biblical genealogies, though no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Zimri's significance lies primarily in his genealogical mention within the tribe of Benjamin, highlighting the preservation of Israel's tribal heritage through careful record-keeping. While no direct narrative role or spiritual significance is attributed to him, his inclusion in Scripture underscores God's providential care in maintaining the lineage of His people. This serves as a reminder of the importance of each individual within God's sovereign plan, even those not prominently featured in biblical events.
